We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.

 Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

#### Explore other styles:

Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the[Interactions API](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview).

When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

## How it works

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a `tool_search` tool to your request and set `defer_loading: true` on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

```py
from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

tools = [
   {"type": "tool_search"},
   {
       "type": "function",
       "name": "issue_refund",
       "description": "Refund an order to the original payment method.",
       "defer_loading": True,
       "parameters": {
           "type": "object",
           "properties": {
               "order_id": {"type": "string"},
               "amount": {"type": "number"},
           },
           "required": ["order_id", "amount"],
       },
   },
   # ... 50+ other deferred functions (leave frequent tools undeferred)
]

interaction = client.interactions.create(
   model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
   input="Order A-1042 arrived damaged. Please refund 40 dollars.",
   tools=tools,
)
```

Inside that single API call, the model searches for `issue_refund`, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the `function_call`. All three steps appear in `interaction.steps`, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions:

```js
"steps": [
 {
   "type": "tool_search_call",
   "id": "tsc_7f2a",
   "arguments": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]},
   "signature": "..."
 },
 {
   "type": "tool_search_result",
   "call_id": "tsc_7f2a",
   "result": [{"type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}],
   "signature": "..."
 },
 {
   "type": "function_call",
   "id": "fc_91c3",
   "name": "issue_refund",
   "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40}
 }
]
```

From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a `function_result`.

There's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the new tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail.

Tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn.

Tool Retrieval also works with [remote MCP servers in the Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling#mcp). Set `defer_loading: true` on an `mcp_server` tool and every tool that server exposes is loaded on demand, so you can connect a large server without listing its tools one by one.

## How client-side retrieval works

If you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the `tool_search` with `"execution": "client"` and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose new tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration:

```py
tools = [{
    "type": "tool_search",
    "execution": "client",
    "name": "search_tools",
    "description": "Search the internal tool registry for functions.",
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["query"],
    },
}]

# When the model emits a function_call for "search_tools",
# return matching {"type": "function", ...} schemas in function_result:
followup = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    previous_interaction_id=interaction.id,
    tools=tools,
    input=[{
        "type": "function_result",
        "name": "search_tools",
        "call_id": step.id,
        "result": my_registry.search(**step.arguments),
    }],
)
```

## How pricing and supported models work

Tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on `tool_search` adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic.

Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including [all Gemini 4 models](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/latest-model), in the Interactions API.

articles.content:
Title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/microsoft-ignite-accelerated-computing-azure-windows-pcs/

Published Time: 2026-11-19T20:00:15+00:00

Markdown Content:
NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs.

At [Microsoft Ignite](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/events/microsoft-ignite/), the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data.

Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including [NVIDIA Dynamo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/dynamo/) inference software for post-training and [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/professional-desktop-gpus/rtx-pro-6000-family/) for Bing search models.

## **NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure**

NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers, providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference.

Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information.

[NVIDIA Confidential Computing](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/solutions/confidential-computing/) and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure.

To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using [NVIDIA MaxLPS](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/maxlps/).

Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In [MLPerf Training v6.1](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/mlperf-training-endpoints-vera-rubin/), Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In [MLPerf Inference v6.1](https://signal65.com/research/ai/microsoft-azure-leads-deepseek-r1-interactive-inference-in-mlperf-v6-1/), Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65.

## **Helping Enterprises Customize and Deploy Open Models**

Enterprise AI agents need to reason through complex tasks, find relevant company information and understand business documents. NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding the models and services available through Microsoft Foundry to help developers bring these capabilities into business applications.

Microsoft’s serverless Programmed Training offering gives developers control over post-training workflows while Foundry manages the underlying infrastructure. Enterprises can focus on their business data, evaluating model responses and improving model behavior.

Foundry Managed Compute adds support for deploying custom model weights, helping connect model customization with deployment through Microsoft’s managed services.

[EY](https://www.ey.com/en_us) used Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry to adapt NVIDIA Nemotron open models for classifying corporate purchasing records, improving accuracy on its evaluation dataset by 55% and lowering cost by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models. The work demonstrates how enterprises can customize open models for specialized business tasks.

The expanded NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 lineup on Foundry Managed Compute supports different requirements across enterprise applications. Nemotron 3.5 Super is designed for long-running agents working across coding, research and business workflows, while Lightning supports applications that need fast responses and tool use.

Complementary models help agents find relevant information with Nemotron Embed and Rerank, extract structured information from documents with Nemotron Parse and detect harmful content with Nemotron Content Safety. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — designed for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning — and Transcribe, for speech recognition, are coming soon.

## **Bringing AI Closer to Enterprise Data**

NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding deployment options beyond the cloud, helping organizations run models and agents closer to their data while maintaining control over their infrastructure and operations.

Expanded support for Nemotron 3.5 in Foundry Local brings capabilities for reasoning, coding and tool-using agents to Azure Local environments. Retrieval models help applications find evidence across text, document images, charts and tables.

Azure Local will also support NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs from hardware partners, giving organizations additional options for deploying AI on premises.

Azure Local is expanding to [NVIDIA Jetson Thor](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-thor/) and [Jetson Orin](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/autonomous-machines/embedded-systems/jetson-orin/) edge AI platforms to support industrial applications such as machine vision, robotics and autonomous operations. NVIDIA physical AI models, including [Cosmos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/), are also being brought to Foundry Local.

On Windows PCs powered by [NVIDIA RTX Spark](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/rtx-spark/), NVIDIA and Microsoft will showcase local large language model experiences at Ignite, demonstrating how developers can run AI applications directly on devices.

For organizations using Cloud PCs, the companies are bringing Direct Stream capabilities to GPU-accelerated Windows 365 Cloud PCs. These capabilities support demanding graphics applications with up to two 4K streams at 60 frames per second and low latency, even over challenging networks. A limited preview is open for sign-ups, with public preview planned for early 2027.

## **Connecting Scientific AI With Microsoft Discovery**

For scientific research, [NVIDIA BioNemo Agent Toolkit](https://github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo/bionemo-agent-toolkit) and [NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvalchemi-toolkit) are[expanding into the Microsoft Discovery catalog](https://aka.ms/Discovery-BioNeMo), bringing models for life sciences, drug discovery and materials and chemical science into Microsoft’s agentic research platform.

BioNeMo Agent Toolkit helps scientists use natural language to run computational biology workflows in Microsoft Discovery, with agents coordinating the tools and model calls needed to carry out the work.

An initial [integration uses the RFD4-Proteina model](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/healthcare-and-life-sciences-leaders-build-on-nvidia-to-advance-drug-discovery-and-expand-patient-care), developed in collaboration with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, to generate candidate protein structures and amino acid sequences for further evaluation and laboratory validation.

## **Accelerating Microsoft’s Models and Services**

Alongside expanding customer access to NVIDIA technologies, Microsoft is using NVIDIA software and accelerated computing in its own AI development and services.

Microsoft AI uses NVIDIA Dynamo to support reinforcement learning rollout inference during post-training. This computationally intensive process generates the experiences used to improve models.

Dynamo coordinates inference across a large GPU fleet, optimizing performance, as well as helping manage requests, model updates and recovery from failures. The deployment builds on joint engineering between Microsoft AI and NVIDIA.

Title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/

Published Time: 2026-11-19T17:00:35+00:00

Markdown Content:
Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with[NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs.

Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities.

Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem.

* * *

## **Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#autonomous-operations)

Video Player

AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build [digital twins](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/digital-twin/) that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions.

Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation.

AI agents built on Falkor’s agentic engine understand dense technical documentation, spatial relationships and real-world physics. Engineers can create and test plans in simulation before traveling on site, reducing costly delays and mistakes. They can also inspect equipment and check clearances in a shared view.

_Read_[_Falkor’s article_](https://falkor.com/blog/from-geometry-to-reasoning)_and_[_watch the livestream_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I4X91GKLgNk)_f_ _or a closer look at how the company builds these tools and checks the agents’ work._

* * *

## **Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation With SimReady Assets**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#pick-and-place)

Getting a robot model into a scene is only the start. Developers also need to assemble its components, add controls and check whether it can complete a task.

NVIDIA developers Dillon Bailey and Rishabh Chadha used 3D assets from the [SimReady Central](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/simready-central-library) library to build a pick-and-place simulation of a robot moving a can using the [NVIDIA Isaac Sim](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/introduction/quickstart_index.html) framework. They directed an agent equipped with GPT-6 Sol and Isaac Sim skills to assemble the scene and generate pick-and-place controls.

Testing the assembled scene shows how the assets work together, from joint movement and contact behavior to the gripper’s ability to hold, move and release the can. With that baseline in place, developers can adjust object positions and motion paths and repeat the tests to evaluate how each change affects the task.

[_Follow the walkthrough_](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/simready-assets-robot-pick-and-place)_to assemble and test a pick-and-place simulation in Isaac Sim, with sample agent prompts and checks for robot movement and grasp behavior._

* * *

## **Build a Voice-Controlled VR Simulation With SimReady Assets**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#vr-simulation)

Bringing 3D assets into virtual reality (VR) requires more than rendering a scene. Objects need to respond to controllers and behave as expected when grabbed, moved or released.

NVIDIA Omniverse community developer Michael Wagner took on this challenge. He directed GPT-6 Astra to use [Blender](https://www.blender.org/) software to model a study environment from two reference images, balancing visual quality with efficient performance in VR.

He then used Claude Code to build an application that lets users find SimReady Central assets by voice and interact with them in an immersive VR scene. The Claude Code agent worked for about eight hours, and Wagner built the application over a weekend using an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada workstation and a Meta Quest 3 VR headset.

The application ran on [NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse): [ovstage](https://github.com/nvidia-omniverse/ovstage) shared the OpenUSD scene, [ovrtx](https://github.com/nvidia-omniverse/ovrtx) rendered it, [ovxr](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovxr)enabled VR and [ovphysx](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/PhysX/tree/main/ovphysx) ran physics. Wagner later built a second version with [ovnewton](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovnewton), which integrates with ovstage, to compare the physics libraries.

The biggest challenge for Wagner was checking what happened inside the headset. Automated tests missed problems he could feel, including objects shaking when grabbed. Wagner reported the symptoms, guided the agent through changes and verified the interaction himself. Updating the grab control once per frame resolved the shaking. His takeaway: Give agents renders and logs to inspect, then check the experience directly.

_Explore his_[_open source demo_](https://github.com/perfectproducts/ovxr_simready_physx_demo)_f_ _or build instructions, a starting prompt and reusable agent skills._

* * *

## **Send Microducks on Rounds in a Simulated Hospital**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#send-microducks)

Video Player

Before adapting a robot to a new environment, developers need to test whether its walking policy — the AI that controls how it moves — can keep it stable in that setting.

AI developer Maziyar Panahi directed Claude Code, using Claude Opus 5.5, to assemble an intensive care unit from 13 [NVIDIA SimReady](https://huggingface.co/spaces/nvidia/simready-central) hospital assets and test Microduck robots inside it. The assets came with [Newton physics](https://developer.nvidia.com/newton-physics) settings, so Panahi didn’t have to model the furniture or create collision geometry from scratch. The Newton physics engine also helped replicate the ward so hundreds of copies could run together on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU.

When the cloud containers lacked graphics support, Panahi and the Claude Code agent separated simulation from rendering, recording robot poses in the cloud and rendering them locally. They also treated the furniture as static collision objects, which enabled larger runs within the solver’s limits.

The robots walked using AI they had already been trained on and followed preset points along a route. Panahi checked how many robots remained upright: In a 256-ward run, 766 of 768 Microducks were still standing after 14 simulated seconds. He said the agent’s work took about two hours.

[_Explore the open source demo_](https://github.com/maziyarpanahi/ai-demos/tree/main/omniverse/simulate-robots-in-an-icu)_for a starter prompt, checks and instructions to begin with one ward on a CPU, then scale to hundreds on an NVIDIA GPU._

* * *

## **Create Editable 3D Assets With Houdini and AI Agents**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#editable-assets)

Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses[SideFX Houdini](https://www.sidefx.com/products/houdini/) and the[NVIDIA ovrtx library](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx) to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance.

In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the[OpenUSD](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/openusd/) framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering.

Scarcella also used a publicly shared robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim, directing the motion and developing materials and lighting in Houdini with Claude’s assistance. Working with team member Steven Dvornik, the team created an “Echos” visualization: translucent versions of the hand overlap and merge into a single hand animation, offering a visual interpretation of robot training.

Video Player

_Figure: An artistic visualization of simulated robot-hand motion, developed with AI assistance and Houdini’s materials and lighting tools._

These workflows bring agent-assisted creation into existing artist tools, giving teams editable content they can inspect, refine and render across applications.

_Explore Scarcella’s[Houdini MCP tools and agent skill](https://github.com/nscrdev/nscr-houdini-mcp)._

* * *

## **Test Robotic Disassembly With Computer-Aided Design and Simulation**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#robotic-disassembly)

Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in [NVIDIA](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim/) Isaac Sim.

Jebens used simulation feedback to revise the tooling, including a wrench designed to reach the suspension’s bolts, and reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation.

Video Player

PTC also [connects computer-aided design](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/computer-aided-engineering/) (CAD) with simulation through Onshape’s SimReady Publisher, built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. [Robotics startup Sensori](https://sensorirobotics.com/) uses it to transfer its Yuri robot into Isaac Sim, carrying geometry, joints and configuration data so the team can evaluate design changes without repeatedly rebuilding the simulation model.

_[Read Sensori’s story](https://www.onshape.com/en/blog/robotics-startup-sensori-cloud-native-cad-nvidia-isaac-sim-physical-ai)._

_[Explore the Onshape importer guide.](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/extensions/latest/ext\_onshape.html)_

* * *

## **Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#building-model)

Video Player

Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation.

David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes.

Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. [OpenUSD](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/openusd/) stores the models, while [Omniverse’s ovrtx library](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx) renders results

Title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-black-friday-2026/

Published Time: 2026-11-19T14:00:12+00:00

Markdown Content:
[GeForce NOW](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/) is kicking off Black Friday with more reasons to make time for gaming. Six-month memberships are back for a limited time. Save 30% on the first six-month term of a [Performance or Ultimate membership](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/). Big gaming plans, smaller price tag.

Keep the holiday savings going: Check out more [NVIDIA holiday deals](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/holiday/) for gamers, creators and AI enthusiasts.

The living room gets a little more playtime, too. GeForce NOW arrives on Amazon Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) running Vega OS, alongside an Amazon offer launching later today for 90% off the first month of an eligible Performance or Ultimate membership in participating countries. It brings console-style gaming to the TV, straight from the Amazon cart.

Bethesda fans have more in store, with five favorites adding GOG support as part of nine games joining GeForce NOW this week.

## **Big RTX Power, Black Friday Price**

Thousands of games are calling from the cloud.

Six-month Performance and Ultimate memberships are back for Black Friday, with 30% off the first six months for new memberships and eligible upgrades in select regions. The sale runs through Monday, Nov. 30, while supplies last.

Go [Ultimate](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) for GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, Steam Deck and other supported handhelds, browsers, mobile devices, compatible TVs and [more](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/system-reqs/). Ultimate brings the latest NVIDIA innovations to the cloud, including DLSS 5 technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature for lifelike lighting and materials in[_NBA 2K27_](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-september-2026-games-list/) and[_Hogwarts Legacy_](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-hogwarts-legacy-dlss-5/), with support coming to[_War Thunder_ and _Where Winds Meet_](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/hogwarts-legacy-war-thunder-dlss-5-3d-guided-neural-rendering/).

The experience goes big with streaming at up to 5K resolution or up to 360 frames per second, plus high dynamic range, ultrawide support and saved in-game settings. DLSS Super Resolution, Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction enhance supported games, including the path-traced missions of [_007 First Light_](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-007-first-light-launch/) and the reality-bending action of [_CONTROL Resonant_](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-control-resonant/), while NVIDIA Reflex and Cloud G-SYNC technologies help keep gameplay responsive and smooth.

GeForce NOW handles downloads, patches and updates for Ready-to-Play games, freeing local storage and leaving more time for gaming.[Choose a membership](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) and start the season streaming.

## **More Screens, Major Savings**

Press play on more possibilities.

GeForce NOW officially expands to all three of Amazon’s Vega OS streaming media players including Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) bringing thousands of [supported games](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/) to more another screens in the home. Vega OS keeps Fire TV fast and responsive, so launching GeForce NOW and jumping into games feels quick and snappy, with no console required.

Getting started is simple: download the GeForce NOW app on a[supported Fire TV device](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/system-reqs/), sign in and connect a compatible controller. From cozy stories to epic adventures, turn-based tactics to co-op challenges, there’s plenty to build, explore and share with friends — all from the comfort of the couch.

There’s a fire deal to get the games going, too. Launching later today through Thursday, Dec. 31, get 90% off the first month of a[Performance or Ultimate membership](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) purchased[directly through Amazon](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-call-of-duty-modern-warfare-4/) on supported Fire TV devices in participating regions. The cloud is ready. The next quest is calling.

Five favorite worlds. Extra ways to play.

Five Bethesda titles expand their GeForce NOW support this week with their GOG versions: _Indiana Jones and the Great Circle_, _Fallout 4_, _The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim_, _DOOM_ and _DOOM Eternal_.

For a faster change of pace, _DOOM_ brings relentless enemies, destructive weapons and fast-moving first-person combat, while its sequel, _DOOM Eternal_, turns up the intensity as the Slayer takes on demonic forces.

Members who own the newly supported GOG versions can stream those titles through GeForce NOW without purchasing them again. From treasure hunts to dragon hunts, the collection can follow across nearly any supported device. Familiar worlds, with a little more room to roam.

Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles.

articles.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
articles.summary: The iPhone maker appears to be building agents that can compete with the likes of Meta Muse, Instinct, Claude, and OpenAI Dots.
articles.content:
Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.
The news was
originally reported
by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”
“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”
The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.”
TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.
Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to
expand its AI offerings
in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.
Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the company is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.
The outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple
issued a notification
to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”
Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”

articles.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
articles.summary: At the upgraded $83/share IPO price, Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million, while the company nabbed nearly $105 billion.
articles.content:
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them
ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece
to sell in the IPO.
At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.
Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company
to philanthropy.
However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”
With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.
$104.8 billion.
That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.
Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.
Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012,
it raised $16 billion on IPO day.
28% stake to Amazon and Google combined.
All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic
because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup,
it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.
The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.
More than
$1 trillion.
As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.
Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.
All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

articles.summary: Meta hasn't denied the reporting from The Information, saying only that it will "have more to share soon" about its upcoming AI wearable.
articles.content:
In Brief
Posted:
1:58 PM PST · November 19, 2026
Image Credits:
Meta/screenshot /
Lucas Ropek
Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300
Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has
reported
.
When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”
So far, Meta has made a
relatively successful push
into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with
a variety of cute avatars
that users can use to give the system more of a personality.

a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49.
Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

articles.title: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
articles.summary: Are the recent outages in the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms really a coincidence? There's actually likely something deeper going on, cybersecurity experts say.
articles.content:
It’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms. In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life.
Apple Pay
went down.
NASA’s
internal communication
network went down. The
FAA had to ground
all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit
with an outage
that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days.
The first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to
attack fridges in a grocery store
and
a blood bank
in France a few weeks ago. Here in the U.S., the director of National Intelligence said these outages
don’t seem related
to state-sponsored terrorism, while President Trump called the issues
“individual events.”
Many of the companies
themselves have said
the outages were not caused by cyberattacks or AI attacks, but tech issues.
Only, there’s the fact that they all struck within a short timespan of each other, and just a few weeks after Cybersecurity’s so-called
“Black October,”
when a slew of also-unrelated cybersecurity
incidents occurred on October 21, striking PHP, Node.js, LiteLLM, more.
While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly.
Dave DeWalt, an investor who worked in cybersecurity for more than three decades (including as president and CEO of McAfee and as vice chairman of the CISA Advisory Council for the Department of Homeland Security), also thinks it’s probably AI-related.
The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch.
The thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he said.
This was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch. “These industrial systems were never designed to be connected, let alone securely connected in the way we are pushing them to be today,” she said.
Virginia Senator Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intel Committee, came to a similar conclusion (although investigations are still underway as to what could be happening). “These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” the senator
wrote on X
.
AI is reshaping how software is built, deployed, and operated, on a scale where everyone feels the sharp learning curve. Iyer cited the FAA outage as an example of legacy tech that is not as sophisticated or advanced as the technologies companies are trying to merge it with.
In less technical terms, she said the outage may have been caused (and preliminary findings point to this) when the FAA was
trying to modernize
its telecommunications infrastructure and the transition overwhelmed parts of its legacy hardware, where the new tech likely operated at a normal modern capacity while the legacy hardware couldn’t keep up.
When looked at this way, she said, AI is actually getting the bad rep. “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. “The fault is the rushed mix of the legacy and modern systems without a clear understanding of operational and cyber risk or the ability to gatekeep and protect the legacy systems.”
Organizations need a more steadfast approach to AI adoption, including more testing and prioritizing what needs to be fixed and when, DeWalt said.
Iyer added, “These industrial systems need to be segmented more tightly and more access controlled, so as modern systems are introduced, it can be phased in and risk mitigated.”
Actually, there might be a silver lining to all of this for companies (and for venture investors). DeWalt said he’d rather see these U.S. enterprises find and patch their flaws, even in this messy way, than have bad actors find and exploit those vulnerabilities in AI warfare that could cause even more national security issues.
And maybe some aspiring founders were inspired by them. DeWalt expects a rise in companies focused on “AI-driven vulnerability management, autonomous remediation, safe patch testing and deployment, and resilience for the systems that keep critical infrastructure running,” he said.
“There’s real pain in this transition as we’ve seen in the past week,” DeWalt said. “But there’s also enormous opportunity for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.content:
Nvidia co-founder and now
former
CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he
cheated on his wife
of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is
a Chinese spy
who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly
purchased
$4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company,
The New York Times
has reported.
The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also
had an extramarital relationship
with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
By early Thursday morning, Huang was
no longer CEO
of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another
extramarital affair
with another unnamed Nvidia employee.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 17, 2026: Nvidia posts strong quarterly earnings, says it does not plan to reinstate Huang
Nvidia reported its
quarterly earnings
on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.
“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress said. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”
Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is
not considering
reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.
November 17, 2026: Huang says he sees ‘outpouring’ of calls for him to return, says he ‘would be honored’ to return as CEO
Jensen Huang posted
his first public statement
since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.
Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder
Palmer Luckey
, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an…
— Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang)
November 17, 2026
November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’
More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.
Bloomberg
reported
that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
Separately, The Wall Street Journal
reported
that Huang had been
critical
of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.
November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee
In a
scathing letter
sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.
“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.
That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.
“The American people deserve answers,” Scott
wrote
on X.
November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters
After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.
November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress
Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO,
Colette Kress
, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
Later in the day, Huang
confirmed
that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell
about 8%
in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he
has said
. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times
reported
that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be
subpoenaed
.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of
upcoming speaking engagements
at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips,
The Information reported
. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International,
Bloomberg reported
. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs,
the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump
weighed in
on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang
should remain chief of Nvidia
, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a
letter
to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid
over 5%
the following day.

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO could deliver $156B to charity
articles.summary: At a stock price of $95, the frontier lab's Public Benefit Foundation, its employee donations, and the company's match tot up to $156 billion.
articles.content:
Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO has made quite a few people generationally wealthy, but it will also be an enormous windfall for the causes backed by the frontier lab and its employees.
As you might expect from a company whose leadership emerged from the world of effective altruism (EA), Anthropic has multiple different avenues for cash raised in its market debut to be directed to philanthropy.
First, the company’s Public Benefit Fund, or PBF (analogous to OpenAI’s foundation), was allotted 5% of the company’s shares, almost 850 million. At the current trading price of about $95, that will leave it with an endowment of $80 billion. And if the company continues its astonishing growth rate, Anthropic could add further 2% increases every time the company’s valuation grows more than 50% over the IPO price of $83, or about $124.50 per share for the next threshold.
The PBF’s money will be focused on research and activities related to increasing the benefit of artificial intelligence to humanity. The
first commitment
of the PBF was $200 million to study the impact of AI on workers; Anthropic has said it will consider donations to philanthropic organizations or “direct distributions to specific populations” — perhaps a hint of future UBI plans.
Anthropic also
donated $50 million
to the city of San Francisco last week. A company spokesperson tells TechCrunch the donation did not come from the PBF.
Next, Anthropic’s employees have pledged shares to philanthropic causes of their choice, and the company will match those donations 3-to-1 for longer tenured employees and 1-to-1 for newer ones. In its S-1 filing, the company said that it had reserved more than 550 million shares to fulfill pledges made before September 30.
Working backwards from that figure, and based on the disclosure that 84% of the shares were reserved for early employee matches, we can estimate that employees have pledged $23 billion of donations; the company’s match on those would be roughly $53 billion, depending on the stock price when those matches are delivered.
All told, it adds up to $156 billion — a huge amount of potential philanthropy. For context, Americans donated $617 billion to charity in 2025; if all of the pledged funds resulting from today’s transactions get to do-gooders, that will be equal to about a quarter of all U.S. donations made last year.
Employees will need to make good on their pledges for this to work out, and the value of the match will ultimately depend on when Anthropic makes its donation. The shares could also go to donor-advised funds, which would likely limit their initial impact.
Interviews with
employees
and
institutions
suggest that donors are most likely to support EA-inflected charities like
Longview Philanthropy
,
GiveWell
,
Coefficient Giving
,
Foresight Institute
, and
Giving What We Can
. And it seems likely that significant funding will be allocated to AI safety research, given the concerns expressed about that subject by many Anthropic employees.

articles.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
articles.summary: Google's latest update to Gemini brings an AI agent to the Mac that can organize files, fill out forms, and tackle multistep workflows.
articles.content:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.
The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google
only this week announced
the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.
Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try
its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September
, which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.
Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.
As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.
Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.
The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a new
Reuters
report that looked at internal company posts.
In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them.
One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”
In another example, an employee using the AI agent on her personal phone received a reminder from Muse to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, the popular end-to-end encrypted messaging app.
“This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post, according to the report.
“Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products,” a Meta spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”
Launched in September, Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps on record, with more than 10 million downloads.

articles.title: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
articles.summary: Everful has raised $48.5 million to expand its factory-direct sourcing platform, helping retailers source products from overseas manufacturers.
articles.content:
Everful
, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.
The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.
Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch, co-founder Sisi Song said. The company ships over 5 million items a month to customers in more than 60 countries and works with over 30,000 factory partners, she added. Its online wholesale catalog includes more than 20 million products.
Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.
Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.
The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.
“We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”
Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.
Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.
Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song said the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical issues since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.
She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of
the de minimis exemption
, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.
Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”
Everful plans to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.
The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

articles.title: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development
articles.summary: In his Nasdaq opening bell speech, Dario Amodei reiterated Anthropic's commitment to pacing AI development, regardless of business or political pressure.
articles.content:
As Anthropic made its Wall Street debut on Thursday in the largest IPO in history, CEO Dario Amodei reaffirmed the company’s commitment to developing AI responsibly. In his speech ahead of the Nasdaq opening bell, Amodei vowed that the AI company would not bend to either business or political pressure and would “remain under human control.”
Reading the speech from a printout, the CEO began by talking about Anthropic’s origins as a way to build powerful technology to help humanity — something that he said was inspired by the loss of his father to a disease that became curable just a few years later.
He acknowledged that while human intelligence had made diseases like the plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world, there were still too few scientists with too little time to make progress in other areas of disease. AI, he said, could help with this by working in concert with humans to further medical progress.
It’s telling that Amodei began with a story highlighting AI’s potentially lifesaving applications, since
he’s warned repeatedly
about the risks of advancing the technology too quickly. In September, Amodei drew headlines when he
outlined a plan to pace AI development
, which included things like coordinating with other leading companies on safety standards and embedding evaluators from third-party organizations to verify that companies were following their safety commitments.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, and xAI owner Elon Musk
said they agreed
with Amodei’s position, although few concrete commitments have been made.
In this morning’s speech, Amodei again stressed the need to progress AI technology and the safety required in doing so. He referred to the “very real risks” of AI in the hands of bad actors, whether those were individuals or nation-states, and the potential for things like “economic disruption” and “losing control of AI systems.”
Anthropic believes these risks are avoidable, he noted, as long as there are safeguards in place. Amodei said the company would continue to be invested in the work of AI alignment and testing, and developing new ways to understand AI behavior so it could remain under human control.
“There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us,” he said. “The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed more so than it has already towards double and triple checking that those AI systems are safe and remain under human control.”
“And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei concluded.
His sister, Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei, echoed these sentiments in an
interview with CNBC
on Thursday, noting that while the risks were real, the promise of AI was also “incredible.”
“We were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks, and I think we have to date done an incredible job doing that. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety,” she added.
The full text of Dario Amodei’s opening speech is below:
Thank you, Daniela. My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind. Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that just a few years later became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments. So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket — tools for gene editing, tools for gene synthesis, tools for controlling brain cells with light — started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking, from intelligence.
Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress in other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades. It took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR. Nature is full of these patterns, but we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them. Too few scientists with too [little] time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would have taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.
I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point, all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time, and although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe these processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by a few years. Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many other applications of Claude. Our customers, the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people, are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth, lift people out of poverty, protect democracy and free societies, even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them, and I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.
At the same time, we’ve always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or by nation-states to economic disruption to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable and we are building anyway, but because we think they are avoidable and we can avoid them. Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic’s DNA from the start, from safeguards against biological and cyber risks to alignment training and testing to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI and keeping it under human control. There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us, the incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed more so than it has already towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and remain under human control.
And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control, we will not bend to either business nor political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing. If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top.
When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models. Everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so. But the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time. The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better. Thank you.
